title: How far does the cyclist go in four hours at the same speed?
description: Meera watches a cyclist on a village road. The video adds hour by hour and then multiplies to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: each hour adds the same distance. Watch for children who add the hours to the kilometres.

video_script.why: The child must find the distance covered in several hours at the same speed.
video_script.substitution: Add the one hour distance for each hour, then check by multiplying the one hour distance by the number of hours.
video_script.anchor: Meera watching a cyclist on a backwater road near Thrissur
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu adds the four hours to the fifteen kilometres. Four counts the hours, and fifteen more kilometres come with each hour.
video_script.payoff_line: she covers sixty kilometres in four hours
maths_rules: speed: 15 km in 1 hour, same speed all the time
video_script.design: One idea: each hour adds the same distance. Wrong idea: add the hours to the kilometres. The cyclist and road stay in the anchor band; the hint card leaves at the break.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the bicycle on the backwater road sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a cyclist on a road; a marker reads 15 km in 1 hour; an empty bracket waits for 4 hours

marks.m63: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m64: a cyclist appears on a road beside water
marks.m65: a marker reading 15 km in 1 hour appears
marks.m66: an empty bracket appears over four hours of road

narration: <bookmark mark='m63'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m64'/>Meera watches a cyclist ride along a backwater road near Thrissur.
<bookmark mark='m65'/>She covers fifteen kilometres in one hour.
<bookmark mark='m66'/>How much distance will she cover in four hours, if she keeps the same speed?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m67: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m67'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a hint card in the working band: think hour by hour; write the total distance after each hour

marks.m68: the words hour by hour light up
marks.m69: the words total after each hour light up

narration: <bookmark mark='m68'/>Think about the distance hour by hour, one hour at a time.
<bookmark mark='m69'/>After each hour, how far has she gone in all so far?
<bookmark mark='m70'/>Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows 15 + 4 = 19; the 4 is circled as hours and the 15 as kilometres; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m72: the 4 is circled as hours and the 15 as kilometres
marks.m73: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour
marks.m74: an arrow shows 15 more km for each hour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m71'/>Fifteen kilometres and four hours make nineteen kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m72'/>Four counts the hours, and fifteen counts the kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m73'/>Hours and kilometres cannot be added together, because they are different things.
<bookmark mark='m74'/>She rides fifteen more kilometres in every hour.

beats.on_screen: four blocks fill with running totals: 15, 30, 45, 60 km; the last total glows

marks.m75: the first block fills with 15 km
marks.m76: the second block fills with 15 + 15 = 30 km
marks.m77: the third block fills with 30 + 15 = 45 km
marks.m78: the fourth block fills with 45 + 15 = 60 km and glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m75'/>After one hour, she has gone fifteen kilometres from the start.
<bookmark mark='m76'/>After two hours, fifteen and fifteen make thirty.
<bookmark mark='m77'/>After three hours, thirty and fifteen make forty five.
<bookmark mark='m78'/>After four hours, forty five and fifteen make sixty, so she covers sixty kilometres in four hours.

beats.on_screen: the four blocks become one line: 15 × 4 = 10 × 4 + 5 × 4 = 40 + 20 = 60 km

marks.m79: the four blocks fold into the line 15 × 4
marks.m81: the line 40 + 20 = 60 km appears and matches the total

narration: <bookmark mark='m79'/>Four hours means that we take four lots of fifteen.
<bookmark mark='m80'/>Multiply ten by four to get forty, and five by four to get twenty.
<bookmark mark='m81'/>Forty and twenty make sixty, which is the same as before.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the cyclist; two check lines appear: add fifteen four times; multiply fifteen by four; both must match
narration: <bookmark mark='m82'/>To check, add fifteen four times, or multiply fifteen by four.
<bookmark mark='m83'/>Both ways must give exactly the same distance.
<bookmark mark='m84'/>The distance must also be more than fifteen, because she rides for more than one hour.
